trial_title: Effectiveness of Vitamin D in Primary Dysmenorrhoea
brief_summary: Vitamin D in the treatment of primary dysmenorrhoea. Design:Randomised controlled trial. Setting:In a university hospital. Population: 142 women aged 16-35 years. Methods: Patients were treated with 667 unit of vitamin D once a day, 200 unit of vitamin E once a day or 400 mg ibuprofen twice a day,2 days before the date of menstruation and continued through the first 3 days, for 2 months. Main outcome measures: Pain score. Results: Mean VAS of vitamin D group was 4,91, was 6,54 in the vitamin E g
